notes:
A literary term where ⟦{百|ひゃく}→百：00780_hyaku⟧ means "all" or "many" (not literally one hundred) and {獣|じゅう} means "beast." Most commonly encountered in the set phrase {百獣|ひゃくじゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{王|おう}→王：19353_ou⟧ (king of beasts).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {百獣|ひゃくじゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{王|おう}→王：19353_ou⟧: king of beasts (referring to the lion)
- {百獣|ひゃくじゅう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{従|したが}える→従える：12561_shitagaeru⟧: to command all beasts

CULTURAL NOTE:
The phrase {百獣|ひゃくじゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{王|おう}→王：19353_ou⟧ appears in anime, manga, and television. The professional wrestler and mixed martial artist Akira Maeda was famously nicknamed {百獣|ひゃくじゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{王|おう}→王：19353_ou⟧. The concept also features in various Japanese card games and fantasy media.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {野獣|やじゅう}: wild beast — refers to specific savage animals
- ⟦{猛獣|もうじゅう}→猛獣：15715_moujuu⟧: fierce beast, dangerous animal — emphasizes danger
- ⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧: animal — the general, everyday word
